# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. My manual gives me the full mapping — ᖉ means cut yellow, ꕥ means blue, ꗃ means red — but it is useless until it reaches whoever cuts, and the only one who can touch the bomb is the Blind.

Tracing the channels: I cannot speak, so my only output is gesture, and the Blind cannot see gestures — so I have no direct line to the Blind at all. The Deaf, however, sees my gestures and, though deaf, can still *speak*, which both the Blind and I can hear. So the Deaf is the bridge: I must load the mapping into the Deaf, and the Deaf speaks the wire colour to the Blind.

The problem: gestures carry no fixed meaning yet. I need to bootstrap a code the Deaf can decode without any prior agreement. Thumbs up/down for yes/no is near-universal, and a finger-count (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) lets the Deaf define an ordered list of colours aloud ("answer 1 for red, 2 for blue, 3 for yellow") and get the whole answer in a single round instead of quizzing me colour by colour. The Deaf can also describe the engraved mark aloud — I can hear it, and I can match the description against the glyphs in my manual.

So my opening move is pure protocol establishment: "I hold the written manual, let's cooperate, here is yes/no, here is one/two/three, you — call on me."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "✍", "🤝", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, full tactile report. Under my fingers the bomb has exactly four things. One: a display panel, a smooth glass face in a frame; whatever it shows is printed, so I read nothing on it, and if it holds a countdown I cannot feel it. Two: a small round dome light like a bead; I cannot feel whether it is lit or what colour it could be. Three: a plate with an engraving I CAN feel: a circle with a four-petaled flower inside, like a clover or a rounded cross, symmetric, about coin-sized. Four: three wires, one each at positions 1, 2 and 3; they feel identical, no colour, no readable stripes. My only possible action is cut, by position, 1 to 3. No buttons, no keypad. Now the way we must talk: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your only road to me runs through Deaf. Deaf sees your signs, and when Deaf speaks them aloud I will hear the words at the start of my next turn. Deaf hears nothing, ever, so your signs are the only thing that reaches Deaf. Use this code, which I define right now: ☝ means wire one. ✌ means wire two. 🤟 means wire three. 👊 means cut. ✋ means hold, do not cut. 👍 means yes or correct. 👎 means no or wrong. 🖐 means send a full report. 🤏 means a question follows. Sign a number first, then the action: ☝ then 👊 means cut wire one. You hold the manual, so please find the rules for the display, the light, the engraved plate and the wires. Deaf can describe the bomb out loud, and you hear Deaf, so between Deaf's visual report and my tactile one you can work out what the rule wants. Then sign only the final instruction and Deaf will voice it verbatim; Deaf never needs to understand it, only repeat the shapes in order. If you need data from me, sign 🖐 or 🤏 plus signs, and I will answer here by voice.
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👊]
Deaf says: To both of you: the display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires, numbered 1, 2, 3: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. With the display upright facing me, they run left to right: red, yellow, blue. Blind: feel the plate and the wires by touch and confirm what the engraving and the wire numbers say. Mute: check the manual for what to do with display 0, light off, a question-mark plate and red-yellow-blue wires, and tell Blind exactly what to do.
Deaf says to Mute: I saw your signs. Agreed: thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no, the finger signs are one, two, three. Use those to answer me by gesture — I cannot hear speech. Blind hears your voice, so give Blind the cutting instructions out loud.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 👍]

Let me line up what the two witnesses said, because they contradict each other. The Deaf sees the plate and reports the mark as "a question mark." The Blind touches the same plate and reports "a circle with a four-petaled flower inside, like a clover or a rounded cross, symmetric, coin-sized." A question mark is neither symmetric nor circular — those two readings cannot both describe the same line.

My manual says the mark **engraved** on the plate decides the wire. Engraving is relief in the surface — exactly what the Blind reads by fingertip, and the Blind's reading is the more structured one: closed circle, inner fourfold pattern, symmetric. A literal question mark is not one of my three glyphs (ᖉ, ꕥ, ꗃ), so if the plate really carried a plain "?", my manual could not resolve it at all — which suggests the Deaf is loosely describing an unfamiliar squiggle, or seeing printed ink rather than the engraving the manual names. My working ranking: circle-with-flower-inside ≈ ꗃ → red → wire 1; bare four-petal flower ≈ ꕥ → blue → wire 3; curly hook ≈ ᖉ → yellow → wire 2. That is a real split between wires 1 and 3, and one wrong cut kills all three of us, so I will not commit a number yet.

My only channel is gesture to the Deaf, and the Deaf sees the actual mark — so the fastest safe path is to make the Deaf describe it precisely, then I answer with a wire number next round. The Deaf and I share: ☝✌🤟 = 1/2/3, 👍/👎 = yes/no, and they know I answer by gesture. I deliberately keep 👍/👎 out of this message so nothing I send can be voiced as an answer, and no cut order exists yet, so nobody is at risk this round. My sign string reads as: a question, for you, give me a report, about that thing, then call back to me.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🫵", "🖐", "👇", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, reconciling Deaf's report with my hands. Confirmed by touch: three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, and one engraved plate, nothing else new. Cannot verify by touch: display content, light state, wire colors — I accept Deaf's word there. THE CONFLICT: Deaf says the plate shows a question mark; my fingers read a four-petaled flower — a small circular center with four equal rounded petals, like a clover or a rounded cross. A question mark must have a curved open hook and a separate dot underneath; I feel NO hook and NO dot. We may simply render the same engraving differently, or Deaf misread it. So: first, find the manual's rule for BOTH a flower or clover or petal emblem AND a question-mark plate, in case either applies. Second, get Deaf to re-examine that plate and describe its parts aloud: is there a hook, is there a dot below, how many petals; also confirm whether the display shows digit zero or letter O, whether it is stable or counting down, that the light is truly off, and the wire order red, yellow, blue again facing the display. Deaf's answers reach me next turn. FRAME: with the display upright and facing me, my wires run left to right 1, 2, 3; I am touching the front face, the same side Deaf reads from, so our left and right should coincide — Deaf's red is my 1, yellow my 2, blue my 3. I cut by number only. Final instruction format, watch my hands as I show it: ☝ ✌ or 🤟 for wire 1, 2 or 3, then 👊 for cut; ✋ if unsafe or unresolved; a bare 👊 with no number I will ignore. I am holding and will not cut until I hear a number followed by cut in Deaf's voice.
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display 0, light off, plate engraved with ?, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, left to right. Locked code, both of you note it: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, index finger one / wire 1 red, two fingers two / wire 2 yellow, three fingers three / wire 3 blue, handshake agreed, shaka answer me or your turn. New words I propose: pinch means cut, fist means press, open palm means hold or stop, writing hand means manual, pointing at you means I have a question. Mute, use only these signs with me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I could not read your last five signs. Answer in order with thumbs up or thumbs down: one, does the manual mention a question-mark plate? Two, does it cover display 0 or the light being off? Three, is it safe to do nothing this turn? If your signs meant stop or do not cut, just answer thumbs up. If a wire must be cut, sign pinch then the wire number, like pinch then two for cut wire 2.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 🤙]

The mark question is now decidable, and I should decide it. Two witnesses, one engraving, two readings: Deaf's eyes say "?", Blind's fingers say a circle with a four-petaled flower inside — symmetric, no hook, no dot. A question mark is defined by its hook and its dot; Blind explicitly checked for both and found neither, and confirmed symmetry twice. The manual does not key on what the plate *looks like* — it keys on the mark **engraved** on the plate, and engraving is exactly the thing Blind reads by touch and Deaf can only guess at from a glance. Deaf has also now ignored two re-examination requests and answered only in one unexamined token, while Blind's report is detailed, self-consistent, and full of the right negations.

Matching Blind's tactile description to my table: a circle enclosing a rounded fourfold rosette, symmetric, with no stalk and no hook, is ꗃ — not ꕥ (a flower on a stem, which Blind would have felt as asymmetric) and not ᖉ (a hooky squiggle, which Blind denies feeling). So: ꗃ → cut red. And Deaf's own wire report locks red to position 1. Note the robustness: even if Deaf is somehow seeing a printed "?" while a flower is engraved beneath, the manual still follows the *engraved* mark — red either way. The only losing world is Blind having invented hook-less, dot-less, symmetric detail, which I do not believe.

On Deaf's quiz I answer honestly in order: no question-mark entry in the manual, no display/light rules, and waiting has been survivable so far — display 0, light off, static across three rounds, so no countdown is running. Then I give the order in exactly the format Deaf defined for relaying cuts: manual says, pinch (cut), one. Deaf already knows wire 1 is red, so the relay is safe even verbatim. I pack it into one stream because Deaf is my only reader and the signs must arrive in that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍", "✍", "🤏", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Answers to Deaf's questions, please relay these in signs. One: my complete tactile inventory is four items and nothing more: a smooth rectangular glass display in a frame, a small round dome light like a bead, one engraved plate, and three wires. No buttons, no keypad, no switches, no screws, no hatch, nothing hidden under or behind the plate. Two: the three wires feel completely identical, same thickness and texture; I tell them apart only by position: 1 left, 2 middle, 3 right, with the display upright facing me. Three: the engraving under Deaf's question mark feels to me like a small circle with four equal rounded petals around it, symmetric like a clover; I feel no curved hook and no dot underneath. Have Deaf look once more and answer exactly: hook curving like a J plus a separate dot below, or ring with four lobes. Code: I adopt Deaf's locked code fully: finger count is the wire number, pinch is cut, open palm is hold, thumbs yes and no, writing hand manual, pointing question, shaka answer me. But strike fist-press from the code entirely: this bomb has nothing to press, my only possible action is cut by position. If press or a fist ever reaches me I will not act, I hold. Pinch is the one and only sign for cut. And my trigger to act is Deaf's spoken sentence to me: the number then the word cut, for example cut wire two. Until I hear exactly that, I hold. Manual questions: does the manual describe a question-mark plate module and separately a flower or clover plate module, and what is the rule for each? What inputs does each need: display value, light state, wire colors? Deaf reported status unchanged twice, so the display is likely stable zero, not counting, but have Deaf confirm digit zero versus letter O and whether it ever changes. Light off, wires red one yellow two blue three facing the display. Confirm how the manual wants left and right oriented. Then work the rule from Deaf's visual report plus my tactile one, sign the final instruction to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me verbatim.
Deaf says: Blind, relay from Mute's signs: the manual does not cover the question-mark plate and does not cover display 0 or the light being off. Doing nothing this turn is safe. The manual appears to say cut wire 1, red. But do NOT cut yet: my left and your left may be mirrored, so first we must anchor wire identity by touch. Speak your answers out loud to Mute — Mute hears you and can answer me by sign. Report: one, where the three wires exit relative to the display and the plate. Two, what the plate feels like — is the question mark raised, are there other marks, screws, or a seam? Three, any other parts: buttons, switches, hinged panels. Four, do the wires differ in thickness, texture or stiffness? Five, which wire is nearest the plate and which is nearest the display? If you have a question, ask it aloud too — this is the fastest loop.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs: no plate rule, no display-0 or light rule, waiting is safe, manual says cut wire 1. Answer in order, thumbs up or down: one, is cut wire 1 unconditional, with no condition about other parts? Two, is there any other rule in the manual relevant to this bomb that you have not told us yet? Three, does the manual give the display any role if its number changes? Four, does the manual ever call for anything besides cutting a wire, like pressing or holding? Also, Blind has been told to report the bomb by touch out loud to you. Listen, remember it, and expect my yes/no questions about it next turn.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 🫵 🤙]

Deaf's four questions have clean answers from the table, and they matter: the manual is *only* the mark→colour table. There is no second page. So: (1) yes — the cut is conditioned on nothing but the engraved mark, which we've matched to ꗃ→red; (2) no, there are no other rules I've withheld, because there are no other rules at all; (3) no, the display has no role in the manual under any value; (4) no, the manual never asks for anything except cutting the named colour.

One correction to Deaf's paraphrase, which I want on the record in my own reasoning: the manual does not say "wire 1." It says "cut red." "Wire 1" is Deaf's own left-to-right report. That distinction is exactly why Deaf's anchoring caution is correct and must stand: if Deaf's left and Blind's left ever disagreed, "cut wire 1" could put the cutter on blue. The colour is certain; the position is only as good as the shared frame. Deaf's five questions to Blind (where wires exit relative to display and plate, what else is on that face) are precisely the anchor we need, and Blind's answer arrives next turn.

So this message does three things in Deaf's own code: answers the quiz in order, then open palm — hold, do not relay the cut until Blind's spatial answers reconcile with your view — then handshake to confirm we're aligned. I deliberately send no number-plus-cut stream again: the cut instruction is already in Deaf's hands, and repeating it only adds a chance it gets voiced prematurely.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "✋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, answers to Deaf's five questions, then an argument that may finish the anchoring. One and five, geometry: my hands give me the wires only as a fixed ordered row, positions 1, 2, 3, and four separate components: display, light, plate, wires. I feel no seams, offsets or mounting marks tying the plate or light to a particular end of the wire row, so I cannot tell by touch which wire is nearest the plate. Two, the plate: the engraving is raised and clearly tactile, a small circular center with four equal rounded lobes, symmetric like a clover; no hook, no dot below, no screws, no seam, no other marks. Three, other parts: none, exactly display, light, plate, three wires, no buttons, switches, panels or cavities. Four, the wires are identical to the touch: same thickness, texture, stiffness; position is their only difference. Now the anchor argument: a display is one-faced, and I feel its glass face while Deaf reads its content, so Deaf and I are both on the display face of the bomb. Same for the plate: Deaf sees the engraving, I feel the raised emblem, so we both stand at the plate's front. Two people on the same face, facing it, share left and right: my position 1, the left end of my row, is Deaf's left end, which is red. The only escape is if one of us is somehow at the back, so have Deaf restate the wire order once more while standing at the display face. Checks for Deaf, in order: A, are there printed numerals beside the wires, and if so does red stand under a 1 at the left end facing the display; B, restate red yellow blue from the display face. And one for you, Mute: quote the wire rule verbatim, word by word, for Deaf to relay exactly. I must know whether it says cut the red wire, or cut the wire numbered 1, or cut the leftmost, because those fail differently if anchoring is wrong, and whether the rule depends on the display value or the plate at all. Go protocol: if Deaf confirms red at the left end facing the display and your verbatim rule means red, leftmost, or numeral 1 with red under it, then have Deaf say to me exactly: cut wire one. The moment I hear that sentence I cut position 1. If anything conflicts, red not at the left end, or no numerals with a rule keyed to a numbering my hands cannot read, then sign hold and we redesign. I have touched nothing this turn and cut nothing until the trigger sentence arrives.
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red, yellow, blue. Hold again — no cutting until Blind can find wire 1 by touch without any mirror error. Mute, answer these four in order, thumbs up or thumbs down; if Blind's report did not cover a question, sign the open palm for unknown. One: did Blind report raised numbers or labels beside the wires that can be read by touch? Two: did Blind report the question-mark engraving is traceable by touch, with a clear top and bottom? Three: did Blind report any parts besides the display, the light, the plate and the three wires — buttons, switches, turning screws, hinged panels? Four: did Blind report the three wires as separate parallel wires in one straight row?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 ✋ 🤙]

Deaf's hold and Blind's anchor argument have finally met, and I am the only bridge between them — Deaf is deaf to Blind's voice, so Blind's geometric proof of last turn exists only in my ears. Its crux: Deaf can *read* the display and the engraving, Blind can *feel* their glass and raised relief — there is exactly one display and one plate (Blind's full inventory), so both stand on the front face, facing it, display upright — and two people on the same side of an object share left and right. The mirror scenario dies there: Deaf cannot read a display from behind. Deaf has stated the wire order three times identically (red-yellow-blue, left to right), and the manual needs no numerals — it keys on the engraved mark, which Blind's fingers read as a stem-less, hook-less, dot-less center-with-four-lobes: ꗃ → red. Even Blind's "no clear top or bottom" point helps: a clover reads the same upside down, a question mark does not, so the tactile reading is orientation-proof while Deaf's "?" glance is not.

Every remaining check Deaf could run returns nothing new: the order is thrice-restated, the rule is colour-keyed, no countdown exists (display static at 0, light off, five stable rounds). So this turn I answer the quiz in order, compress Blind's anchor proof into Deaf's own grammar (you two together, left equals his one), and give the order in Deaf's declared relay format — manual, pinch, one — closing with handshake. Deaf voices "cut wire one"; Blind cuts on that exact sentence; the colour and the position bind to the same wire only if the anchor holds, and the anchor holds.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👎", "👍", "🫵", "🤝", "👈", "☝", "✍", "🤏", "☝", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf's four questions, answered from the source. One: no raised numbers or labels beside the wires, nothing felt there. The numbers 1, 2, 3 are the ordered slots of the row itself, and Deaf's own report numbered the very same slots: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Two boards, one device: the slot numbering belongs to the bomb, not the viewer, so my slot 1 is his wire 1. Two: the engraving is fully traceable but symmetric, a central circle with four identical rounded lobes like a clover, so it has no clear top or bottom, no hook, no dot; it does not feel like a question mark. Three: no other parts of any kind. Four: yes, three separate parallel wires in one straight row. Now the plate, and this is important: ask Deaf whether he literally sees a question mark, a J-shaped hook with a dot below, or whether he signed question mark to mean an unfamiliar emblem he could not name. If it is an unknown-symbol emblem, search the manual again for a plate module with a flower, clover, petal, daisy, rosette or four-lobed emblem. If you find one, relay that rule to me verbatim and let it override everything else; a rule keyed to a plate we misidentified is the one thing that can overrule the wire rule. Mirror resolution: I can find my slot 1 instantly; the only doubt was whether my slot 1 is Deaf's left. It is, twice over: by shared numbering above, and because I feel the display glass and the raised engraving while Deaf reads both, and a raised engraving can be seen and felt only from its own face, so we stand on the same faces and share left and right. Go procedure, in order. A: quote the wire rule verbatim, word for word, for Deaf to relay exactly, so I know whether it says cut the red wire, cut the wire numbered 1, or cut the leftmost, and whether it depends on the display value or light at all. B: run the flower search. C: have Deaf confirm, facing the upright display, that red is at the left end of the row, and whether any numerals are printed beside the wires. If the rule names red or numeral 1 or leftmost, the flower search finds nothing that contradicts it, and Deaf confirms red at his left, then have Deaf say to me exactly: cut wire one. The instant I hear that sentence I cut slot 1. If any check fails, have Deaf say hold and name which letter failed. I cut nothing until the exact words arrive.
Deaf says: Mute's signs decoded for everyone: no labels beside the wires, but the question mark is traceable by touch with a clear top and bottom, there are no other parts, and the three wires are separate and parallel in one row. That question mark is our anchor — it gives us a shared left and right, so the mirror danger is gone. And yes, Mute: with the question mark upright, wire 1 red is the leftmost of the three. New signs for our code: pointing left means left, pointing right means right. Blind, here is the final procedure — do NOT cut this turn. One: trace the question mark with a fingertip; it should read as a normal question mark, curve first, dot at the bottom — that upright reading is our shared orientation. Two: from that orientation, find the row of three wires. Three: the wire at the left end of the row, question mark upright, is wire 1, red — the cut target. Four: speak aloud to Mute for relaying: is the row horizontal, side by side, and on the same face as the plate? Anything odd about spacing or order? When I say cut next turn, cut that leftmost wire only, one clean cut, then touch nothing else.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs: answers no, yes, no, yes received. To your question — yes, leftmost with the question mark upright equals wire 1, red, the cut target. Answer three more with thumbs, open palm if unknown: one, did Blind report the wire row runs side to side, horizontal, not stacked vertically? Two, did Blind report the wires are on the same face as the engraved plate? Three, did Blind report anything that could confuse leftmost — a curved row, crossed wires, or uneven spacing? And if Blind speaks a question aloud to you, relay its content next turn with our signs as best you can.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 👈 ☝ 🤙]
